questions.def: 'Will have finished' indicates future perfect, action completed before another future action.
questions.question: By the time he arrives, we ___ the presentation.

questions.def: 'Haven't seen' uses present perfect to show a continuing state from past to now.
questions.question: I ___ him since he moved to London.

questions.def: 'Had written' uses past perfect, action completed before another past action.
questions.question: He ___ three books before he turned thirty.

questions.def: 'Would have acted' uses conditional perfect, hypothetical past situation.
questions.question: If I had known, I ___ differently.

questions.def: 'Will have been working' indicates future perfect continuous, duration until a future point.
questions.question: By next year, I ___ here for five years.

questions.def: 'Believe' is a stative verb, use 'I believe' instead of continuous.
questions.question: I am believing that he is telling the truth.

questions.def: 'Used to live' expresses a past habit or state that is no longer true.
questions.question: They ___ in Paris when they were younger.

questions.def: 'Has been playing' uses present perfect continuous, ongoing action started in past.
questions.question: She ___ the piano since she was five years old.

questions.def: 'Is supposed' expresses expectation or obligation; future in present.
questions.question: He ___ to finish the report by Friday.

questions.def: 'Have been working' uses present perfect continuous, ongoing action with duration.
questions.question: I ___ on this project for hours.

questions.def: 'Told' is the simple past tense, correct for a completed past action.
questions.question: He ___ me yesterday that he was coming.

questions.def: 'Is going' uses present continuous for future arrangements.
questions.question: She ___ to the conference next week.

questions.def: 'Know' is a stative verb, use 'I have known' instead of continuous.
questions.question: I have been knowing him since we were children.

questions.def: 'Had studied' is past perfect, action completed before another past action.
questions.question: He ___ French before he moved to Paris.

questions.def: 'Had left' uses past perfect, action completed before another past action.
questions.question: The train ___ before we reached the station.

questions.def: 'Had been living' past perfect continuous, duration of action before past point.
questions.question: She ___ in London for ten years before moving to Rome.

questions.def: 'Have been waiting' uses present perfect continuous, action started in past and continues.
questions.question: I ___ for you for an hour.

questions.def: 'Will be going' future continuous, describes ongoing action at future time.
questions.question: By the time you finish, I ___ home.

questions.def: 'Received' uses simple past, completed action in the past.
questions.question: She ___ the job offer last week.

questions.def: 'Think' as opinion is stative; use 'I think' instead of continuous.
questions.question: I am thinking he is a very good person.

questions.def: 'Had met' is past perfect, action completed before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ before at the conference.

questions.def: 'Had left' uses past perfect, necessary for third conditional sentences.
questions.question: If I ___ earlier, I wouldn't have missed the train.

questions.def: 'Will have been working' future perfect continuous, duration up to a future point.
questions.question: He ___ in this company for 20 years next month.

questions.def: 'Have known' uses present perfect, state continuing from past to present.
questions.question: I ___ her since childhood.

questions.def: 'Would have gone' uses the perfect conditional, hypothetical past situation.
questions.question: He ___ to the party if he had finished his work.

questions.def: 'Had already sent' uses past perfect, completed action before another past action.
questions.question: She ___ the email before I did.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had lost' emphasizes completion before the past event.
questions.question: By the time the results were announced, she ___ all hope.

questions.def: Present perfect 'haven't seen' indicates a continuing state from the past.
questions.question: I ___ him since the conference last year.

questions.def: Past continuous 'were living' describes an ongoing action in the past.
questions.question: They ___ in London when the war began.

questions.def: 'Was to' indicates a planned action that did not happen.
questions.question: He ___ the report by Friday, but he missed the deadline.
